clue.text: Soldiers gambled about the final battle before victory

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the soldiers and the gambling word are read backwards together

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers
to dice is to gamble with dice, so gambled gives diced

explanation.surface: Troops who bet on the outcome of the last fight of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run REDICED round, giving DECIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding game or contest, the one that settles who wins, is called this in sport.

clue.text: Rising journalist, well known, is slandered

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, so the journalist's letters go backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
famed means well known

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming famous reporter has been defamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns ED to DE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To defame is to damage someone's reputation, which is what slander does.

clue.text: Putting together a meal

definitions.meaning: collating is gathering and arranging pages or information together

explanation.surface: Preparing food for a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembling pages in order is one sense; a light repast, especially a cold one, is the other.

clue.text: Teachers accept Times leader's prohibitions

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the teachers word holds the next letter inside

parts.note: dons are university teachers

indicators.note: leader's means the first letter of the word Times

explanation.surface: Academics take on a newspaper editorial about bans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times leader is its editorial, but here it means just T, the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Things you must not do are the forbidden list, the rules against.

clue.text: To create trouble, in a race is improper

indicators.note: improper means not in the right form, so the letters of in a race is are rearranged

explanation.surface: Misbehaving during a race is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to cause an uproar comes from the biblical Cain, a byword for violence.

clue.text: Unintentionally drop flag before the start

parts.note: to flag is to tire or decline, and to fall is to decline too
the off is the start of a race, as in 'they're off'

explanation.surface: Someone lets a flag slip from their hands just before a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling from a horse or bike is an accidental drop from it, the idiom for coming off.

clue.text: Side-note in gospel

indicators.note: in says the note goes inside the gospel word

parts.note: gospel truth is plain fact
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A marginal comment in a book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side-note' looks like one word but splits: 'Side' is the definition and 'note' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: One face of a cut gem, or an aspect of a matter, is one of its sides.

clue.text: A great majority of countries lied in negotiation

parts.note: lands are countries

indicators.note: in negotiation suggests terms being worked over, so the letters of lied are rearranged

explanation.surface: Most nations told untruths during diplomatic talks.
explanation.definitionFit: An overwhelming election win is described by this word for a huge majority.

clue.text: References to notes in Anglophobe literature

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the words Anglophobe literature

explanation.surface: Footnote markers in anti-English writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Daggers used in printing to point the reader to footnotes are marks referring to notes.

clue.text: Weakness due to stress in army duty

definitions.meaning: metal ... is weakening caused by repeated stress
menial non-combat tasks given to soldiers

explanation.surface: A soldier worn out by the strain of service.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal weakened by repeated loading has one sense; menial military chores the other.

clue.text: Criminal attacked in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: fell on means set upon, attacked

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker gets verbally assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who commits a serious crime is a criminal by legal definition.

clue.text: Where singers might all come in together

definitions.text: Where singers might all come in together

parts.words: Where singers might all come in together
parts.note: read literally, a choir entering at once; the phrase also names the place they sing, a musical performance, giving the idiom for acting jointly

explanation.surface: A choir hitting its entry on the same beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting jointly is described by an idiom whose literal sense is at a musical performance.

clue.text: It establishes a need for dynamic statesmen

indicators.note: dynamic suggests energetic movement, so the letters of the next word are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A test of need is called for by energetic politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: This British welfare assessment checks income to decide whether someone qualifies for benefits.

clue.text: Attempt to strike Preston's centre -forward

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle letter of the town name Preston

parts.note: in football a winger plays forward, so a forward can be a wing

explanation.surface: A football striker at Preston (a Lancashire town with a league club) takes a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-forward' looks like a football position but splits: 'centre' takes S from Preston, and 'forward' gives WING.
explanation.definitionFit: A swipe or punch aimed at someone is an attempt to hit them.

clue.text: Run in the way

definitions.meaning: to ... a car or business is to run it
a road or private way up to a house

explanation.surface: Someone sprints down the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Run means operate a vehicle; the way means a road or driveway, both senses of one word.

clue.text: Laying out a tenner? It's to throw a party

indicators.note: laying out means arranging, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the word it, with the 's as is joining it to the definition

explanation.surface: Spending ten pounds to host a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laying out' suggests spending money, but signals rearranging A TENNER plus IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosting guests at a party is what it means to receive and amuse people at home.

clue.text: A client finally gets payment for property

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word client

parts.note: a tribute was a payment made by a subject state to a ruler

explanation.surface: A customer at last pays up for a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality or characteristic belonging to something is one of its properties.

clue.text: It's hard to be unhappy when on course, sailing here

indicators.note: unhappy means in a bad state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's of It's supplies the letter S

explanation.surface: Life afloat is too pleasant to be miserable on a set course.
explanation.walkthrough: HARDTOBE and the S from It's are rearranged. THE BROADS are the lakes and rivers of Norfolk, popular for boating holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: This Norfolk waterway network is a famous place for boating holidays.

clue.text: The pursuit of an English country gentleman, according to Wilde

definitions.text: The pursuit of an English country gentleman, according to Wilde

parts.words: The pursuit of an English country gentleman, according to Wilde
parts.note: Oscar Wilde called fox-hunting the unspeakable in full pursuit of the thing that cannot be eaten

explanation.surface: A literary quip about what a squire chases.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox, which nobody would eat, is Wilde's quarry; the word means not fit to be eaten.

clue.text: The Lady of the Lake?

parts.note: not the Arthurian figure but a woman's name shared with a large lake on the German-Swiss-Austrian border

explanation.surface: A reference to the Arthurian enchantress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Constance is the big Alpine lake, and this is also a woman's first name.

clue.text: Hastily snatch the sauce

definitions.meaning: to catch something up is to grab it quickly
a variant spelling of tomato ketchup

explanation.surface: Someone grabs the ketchup bottle in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Grabbing quickly is one sense; a tomato relish spelt as an older variant is the other.

clue.text: Leave by means of following the river

parts.note: the Exe is the river that flows through Exeter in Devon
at can mean by, as in at or by the door

explanation.surface: Departing by walking along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' here is a noun: an exeat is the formal permission a British school or college gives a pupil to be absent for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission for a pupil to be away from school is a formal leave of absence.

clue.text: Check one's fit and see how far one can go

definitions.meaning: to try a garment on is to see if it fits

definitions.text: see how far one can go
definitions.meaning: to test someone's patience or the rules

explanation.surface: Shopping for clothes while testing limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing whether clothes fit is one sense; pushing boundaries cheekily is the other.

clue.text: Keep in a drawer?

definitions.meaning: a keep is the main ... of a castle
a drawer is something that draws or pulls, so one that tows

explanation.surface: Something is stored away in a chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep is a castle stronghold; a drawer is one who pulls along, a towing person or vehicle.

clue.text: Deity, honoured in his day

definitions.meaning: Wednesday is named after this god, so he is honoured in its name

explanation.surface: A god who was revered in his time.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Anglo-Saxon god, equivalent to Odin, gives his name to the middle weekday.

clue.text: Safe to take 'up the strain? Admirable!

parts.note: a strain is a tune or melody, which is an air
worthy means deserving respect, admirable

explanation.surface: A pilot judges whether a plane can bear the stress and finds it excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft fit to fly has been certified as safe to go up.

clue.text: Hack neglecting male point of view

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving out, so the male letter is dropped

parts.note: to hack at something is to mangle it

explanation.surface: A journalist ignores the man's perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist but is the verb meaning MANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular slant or standpoint on a story is the way you look at it.

clue.text: No charge for lecture

parts.note: O is zero, nothing, so no
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A free talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak pompously at length is to hold forth, as in a lecture.

clue.text: Something hard to destroy, holding unlimited hazard in the garden

indicators.note: holding says the first creature keeps the trimmed hazard word inside it

parts.note: the Hydra of myth grew two heads for each one cut off, so it was hard to kill

indicators.note: unlimited means losing its limits, the first and last letters of the hazard word

parts.note: a hazard is a danger

explanation.surface: A hard-to-kill pest lurking somewhere risky in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips DANGER to ANGE, which goes into HYDRA. The definition is loose: 'Something ... in the garden' points to a garden shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering shrub with big round heads of blooms grows in many gardens.

clue.text: Doctor located in island province

indicators.note: located in says the doctor is placed within the island word

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree standing for a doctor

explanation.surface: A physician based on an island region.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means scope or sphere, the range of one's province or field.

clue.text: The punishment for putting a note in the small change

indicators.note: putting one thing in another means it goes inside the coins
putting one thing in another means it goes inside the coins

parts.note: pence are the small coins of British money

explanation.surface: Being fined for slipping a banknote among the coppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-imposed penalty to atone for a wrong is a punishment.

clue.text: Book noticed lying round in illegal drinking establishment

indicators.note: lying round says the seen word sits around the book abbreviation

parts.note: noticed means seen
Heb is the abbreviation for Hebrews, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone spots a book left about in an unlicensed bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a volume left about, but crosswords often mean a book of the Bible; the shebeen is chiefly an Irish and Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish and Scottish word for an unlicensed bar, a place selling liquor illegally.
